Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 96, verse 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

"Iqra'" (Recite): i.e., bring about recitation, which is the gathering of words composed of letters by the tongue.

"Bismi Rabbika" (In the name of your Lord): i.e., by mentioning the name of your Lord.

"Alladhi khalaq" (Who created): i.e., who created Adam from a extract of clay.

"Khalaqa al-insan" (Created man): i.e., the human being, who is the offspring of Adam.

"Min 'alaq" (From a clinging clot): i.e., the plural of 'alaqa, which is the sperm-drop in its second stage, when it becomes an 'alaqa, that is, a piece of thick blood.

"Wa Rabbuka al-Akram" (And your Lord is the Most Generous): i.e., the One for whom there is no equal in generosity, who is not matched or equaled.

"Alladhi 'allama bil-qalam" (Who taught by the pen): i.e., who taught His servants writing and script by the pen.

"'Allama al-insan" (Taught man): i.e., the human species.

"Ma lam ya'lam" (What he did not know): i.e., what he had not known of the other sciences and knowledge.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted said: ﴿Recite in the name of your Lord who created, created man from a clinging clot. Recite, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾. These five verses are the first of what was revealed of the Noble Qur'an, as the authentic hadiths indicate. Among what is well known in this regard is that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to go to Hira' to practise tahannuth (tahannuth: to abandon sin and withdraw from wrongdoing), withdrawing from what his people were upon of shirk and falsehood, until the truth came upon him while he was in the cave of Hira'. He said: "O Muhammad, I am Jibril, and you are the Messenger of God." Then he said: "Recite!" I said: "I am not a reader." He took hold of me and pressed me three times until I reached the limit of exertion, then he said: "Recite in the name of your Lord who created," and I recited...

As for His saying ﴿Recite in the name of your Lord﴾, Allah commands His Messenger to begin his recitation by mentioning the name of his Lord, i.e., "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful." His saying ﴿who created﴾ means He created all creation, created Adam from clay, and created man, the descendants of Adam, from a clinging clot. Al-'alaq is a collective noun whose singular is 'alaqa, a thick piece of blood. During the first forty days in the womb it is a sperm-drop, then it develops into an 'alaqa that clings to the wall of the womb, then in another forty days it develops into a lump of flesh. Then either it is ordained that it be formed and so it is formed, or otherwise the womb expels it as a lump of flesh.

His saying ﴿Recite, and your Lord﴾ is an emphasis of the first command, because of the difficulty of the matter and the Messenger's (ﷺ) bewilderment at the suddenness of the event. ﴿Recite, and your Lord is the Most Generous, who taught by the pen﴾, i.e., your Lord, the Most Generous, is the One who taught His servants writing and script by the pen. His saying ﴿taught man what he did not know﴾ means: out of His generosity, from which He pours forth His countless blessings upon His servants, He taught man by means of the pen what he had not known of sciences and knowledge. This is an exaltation of the pen, that it is the means of sciences and knowledge, and a means takes its honour from the honour of the end it serves. Therefore there is nothing more noble in this world than the righteous servants of Allah, and the divine sciences in the Book and the Sunnah, and what they called to and urged upon of beneficial knowledge for mankind.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of divine revelation and confirmation of Muhammad's prophethood.

2. The legitimacy of beginning recitation by mentioning the name of Allah; for this reason all surahs of the Qur'an except al-Tawba begin with "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."

3. Explanation of the development of the sperm-drop in the womb into an 'alaqa, from which man is formed.

4. Magnifying the majesty of Allah and the greatness of His generosity, so that no one equals Him in generosity.

5. Highlighting the importance of writing and script by the pen, since knowledge and sciences were not recorded except by writing and the pen.

6. Demonstrating Allah's favour upon man in teaching him what he did not know by means of writing and script.

Explanation of the Words:

Kalla: meaning "No" or "Indeed not," a particle of warning and awakening, after which the particle inna takes a kasra (inna is then read as a fresh clause).

Inna al-insan: meaning the son of Adam, before his feelings and character are refined by faith and the lawful etiquette.

Layatgha: meaning he exceeds the limit set for him in his conduct and dealings.

An ra'ahu istagha: meaning when he sees himself made independent by his wealth, his children, or his authority.

Inna ila rabbika ar-rujʻa: meaning indeed, to your Lord, O Messenger, is the return, that is, the coming back and the final destination.

Alladhi yanha 'abdan idha sall: meaning Abu Jahl, 'Amr ibn Hisham al-Makhzumi, may Allah curse him.

In kana 'ala al-huda aw amara bi't-taqwa: meaning he is the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim al-Qurashi al-'Adnani.

In kadhdhaba wa tawalla: meaning he is Abu Jahl.

La'in lam yantahi: meaning from harming our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and from preventing him from praying behind the Maqam.

Lanasfa'an bi'n-nasiyah: meaning we will surely seize him by his forelock and drag him into the Fire of Hell.

Falyad'u nadiyah: meaning the men of his assembly and gathering-place.

Sanad'u az-zabaniyah: meaning the guardians of Hell.

Kalla: meaning let this liar and disbeliever desist.

Waqtarib: meaning draw near to Him, the Exalted, through obedience to Him.

Meaning of the Verses:

The words of the Exalted, "Indeed, [but] man transgresses, in that he sees himself self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return," inform us about the nature of man before faith and divine knowledge, which encompass knowledge of what Allah loves and what displeases Him, refine him. When he sees himself made independent by his wealth, his children, his authority, or all of these, and feels no need of anyone else, he transgresses, going beyond the bounds of good manners, justice, truth, and custom; he becomes arrogant, oppresses, withholds rights, despises the weak, and mocks others. Abu Jahl was the byword for this description of transgression, to the point that it was said he was the Pharaoh of this Ummah. Here was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying in the Sacred Mosque behind the Maqam, when this tyrant came to him, threatened him, and said: "I have forbidden you from praying here, so do not return. If I find you again, I will seize you by the forelock and drag you on the ground." Then Allah the Exalted revealed these verses: "Indeed [but] man transgresses, in that he sees himself self-sufficient." He thereby made His Messenger understand the reality he already knew: that what he suffered from Abu Jahl and his like among the tyrants of Quraysh had a cause, and He consoled him, saying: even if they transgress and act arrogantly, "indeed, to your Lord is the return," O our Messenger. So be patient with their harm and await what will befall them; their final destination is to Us, not to anyone else, and We will avenge you on them. Then He said to him words that lead intelligent people to wonder at Abu Jahl's disgraceful conduct toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?" Does one who prays forbid prayer, is prayer a crime, is there harm in prayer to anyone? How then can he forbid it? He says to him, "Have you seen if he (the one who prays, who is the Messenger himself, ﷺ) is upon guidance," which leads to the happiness and honour of this world and the next? "Or enjoins righteousness," that is, commands others to what protects them from the punishment of this world and the next. Is commanding guidance and piety, that is, the means of salvation and happiness, to be opposed, fought, struck, and threatened? This is truly the most astonishing of wonders.

He says: "Have you seen, O our Messenger, if this one who forbids a servant when he prays denies (the truth and religion) and turns away (from faith and the Law)?" What will his state be on the day he meets his Lord? "Does he not know that Allah sees?" That is, He sees his provocative, detestable deeds, his insolence toward the Messenger of Allah, and his threat to strike him if he finds him praying behind the Maqam. After this call to the tyrant, perhaps he would return to the truth when he hears it, but instead he increased in transgression and said in the assembly of Quraysh: "By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, if I see Muhammad (ﷺ) praying, I will surely step on his neck and rub his face in the dust." And indeed he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was praying, to tread on his neck, but he recoiled on his heels and shielded himself with his hands. He was asked, "What is the matter with you?" He said, "Between me and him is a trench of fire, terror, and wings." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him limb from limb." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: "No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize him by the forelock, a lying, sinful forelock," that is, its owner, Abu Jahl; meaning, if he does not desist from harming Our Messenger and from confronting him in his prayer to stop him from it, We will surely seize him by his forelock and drag him to Hell before everyone's eyes.

"Then let him call his assembly," at that moment, the men of his gathering and his people's council; "We will call the guardians of Hell," that is, the angels who guard the Fire. "No!" Let this tyrant desist, and let him know that he will not be able to reach Our Messenger with harm after today.

After threatening and restraining the tyrant, and he indeed desisted and never again dared to stretch out his tongue or his hand against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Exalted said to His Messenger (ﷺ): "Do not obey him," in what he asks of you, namely abandoning prayer in the Sacred Mosque, for We have sufficed you against his evil. "And draw near," to Us through acts of obedience, the most important of which is prayer.

Guidance from the Verses:

1. Explanation of the cause of revelation of the verses "No! Indeed, man transgresses..." to the end of the surah.
2. Explanation of man's nature when he is not refined by faith and piety.
3. Allah's support of His Messenger (ﷺ) through the angels, visibly, in the Sacred Mosque.
4. Recording Allah's curse upon the Pharaoh of this Ummah, Abu Jahl, and that he was the greatest oppressor among the Quraysh toward the Messenger of Allah and his companions.
5. The prescription of prostration upon reciting this surah: when one recites "Recite and draw near" (al-'Alaq 96:19), prostration is prescribed, except when one is praying in congregation in a silent prayer, in which case one does not prostrate, lest one cause them trial.

Is commanding guidance and piety, that is, the means of salvation and happiness, to be opposed, fought, struck, and threatened? This is truly the most astonishing of wonders.
